sentences: In 1897, the detective receives a letter from his brother asking him and the doctor to investigate a singer performing at a birthday party held by a construction baron for his daughter.
During the party, the baron is shot dead by an unknown assassin.
Working with a police inspector, the detective and the doctor identify two suspects.
One is the daughter, who has a strained relationship with her father.
The other is the baron's partner, who he apparently caught embezzling.
During the investigation, three more corpses are found which are connected.
The first is a bartender at the party.
The second is the baron's lawyer.
The third is an unknown man, later identified as the baron's troubled nephew.
The detective also connects the case to the disappearance of an actress and an actor, actors who co-owned a theatre troupe the baron bought.
Due to their being lovers despite the actress also being in a relationship with the third owner, he was suspected, but ultimately let go.
Eventually, the detective deduces the culprits to be the lieutenant, a soldier in a relationship with the daughter, his manservant, and the nephew.
The manservant is actually the actor, who killed the actress in a jealous rage and convinced the lieutenant to help him disappear.
The two worked with the nephew to take the baron's fortune.
At the party, the actor disguised himself as the lieutenant, allowing the real lieutenant to shoot the baron.
The bartender was killed for recognizing the fake lieutenant.
The nephew tried to steal the baron's will and killed the lawyer when he couldn't find it.
When the lieutenant became engaged to the daughter, the nephew was no longer needed and killed.
The partner meanwhile had embezzled to help families of workers the baron had wronged, which the baron approved of.
The detective tricks the lieutenant into confessing by falsely claiming the police will find evidence of the murders and they're arrested.
The detective and the doctor then prepare to investigate the singer as his brother requested.
This investigation is set on 12 April 1889.
The detective and the doctor learn about a series of mysterious deaths of three men who were part of an archeology trip to the desert country.
Each man was found strangled and found with a sheath of a mummy's wrapping present at each murder.
The newspaper reports the deaths were caused by an ancient mummy, reducing their credibility.

The detective and the doctor decide to take on the case to find the real culprit, but they face a challenge as all three murders were respectively orchestrated in the capital, the desert country and at sea.
This case takes place on 4 July 1888.
A young woman is found hovering over the body of her lover in a hotel in the capital with a pistol in her hand.
She is arrested for her lover's murder, despite having no memory of ever being there, nor purchasing the gun that was bought in her name.
She insists that she is innocent as the detective and the doctor take on the case to see if she is telling the truth.
Along the way, the detective and the doctor learn about her lover's dubious activity at night.
The investigation takes place on 10 June 1890.
An old general is murdered in his home by a mysterious visitor who quickly vanishes from the scene of the crime.

The detective and the doctor investigate to see whether the crime was due to the general's part in a Veteran Tontine lottery, a book he was writing on a missing diamond, a disgruntled marriage, or some hidden scandal deep in his past.

Set in the year 1894 and reaching into 1895 during the time of the earlier game in the series, the overarching plot is that a group of terrorists calling themselves the rebel group are attempting to overthrow the government, and free the people of the country from debt.
The game features six separate cases, some of which are direct adaptations of original canon about the detective by the original author.
Each case is self-contained and apart from in-game achievements, such as moral choices, do not relate to one another.

The cases are as follows: The first case: the detective is engaged by the police inspector to investigate the murder of a seaman, known by a nickname, an ill-tempered whaling captain who was found impaled on the wall of his garden cabin with a whaling harpoon.
The case is an adaptation of "an original story".

This specific case likely takes place either during or after the events of another earlier game, which largely takes place between September and November 1888, as the murder weapon in this case is displayed on the wall of the detective's lodgings, although the doctor refers to the victim in this game as "a variant nickname".
He also mentions how an experiment the detective wants to conduct is similar to one they conducted on "the serial killer case".
The second case: the detective's brother asks him to look into the rebel group, a band of anarchists plotting an attack on the capital.
The detective refuses since he is not interested in politics, and he continues on a trip with the doctor to a rural county.
A week later, the detective and the doctor plan to take a train back to the capital but the train mysteriously vanishes.
They investigate the disappearance of the train.
This story adapts elements from "another original story".
The third case: the police inspector tells the detective about a political incident concerning the rebel group, but the detective again refuses to get involved.
However, he does agree to investigate the murder of a renowned archaeologist who was found dead in the locked steam room of the Roman baths in the capital.
The detective delves into an investigation featuring three suspects and an ancient cult.
The fourth case: a baronet, an aristocrat of violent temper, has allegedly been murdered by a trio of burglars who also took his wife hostage and stole his silverware.
The detective pursues the culprit or culprits while questioning the veracity of the lady's statement.
The story is adapted from "a third original story".
The fifth case: An old friend (from the earlier game in the series) asks the detective to investigate the theft of some exotic plants at the botanical gardens.
The investigation takes a new turn as the Director of the Gardens is revealed to have died a few days before the theft and the detective suddenly finds himself investigating a possible murder.
The sixth case: The older brother of the street boy, the detective's chief street informant, has been charged with double murder and the street boy asks the detective to clear his brother's name.
The case soon begins to have a whole new aspect featuring men who disappear from plain sight.
At the end, the detective confronts the rebel group after learning more about their plan during the last case.
They attempt to reason with him that their goal is for the benefit of the people.
The detective can choose to allow them to carry out their plan, or to stop them, though he will not take them into custody.

Across five linked cases, the detective confronts dark family secrets, both in his cases and personally, when a visiting woman begins interfering in his personal life, especially with his adopted daughter.

Following the events of the previous game, after the criminal mastermind's death, the detective is now taking care of the criminal mastermind's daughter, the girl, while keeping her true origin as a secret.
However, the situation changes when a mysterious woman becomes the detective's new neighbor.
The mysterious woman slowly befriends the girl, eventually earning the daughter's trust while causing emotional issues between the detective and the girl at the same time.
Throughout the game, the detective will solve different cases while getting to know the mysterious woman's origin and her true intention.
The game features five separate cases.
Each case is self-contained and apart from in-game achievements, such as moral choices, do not relate to one another.
The cases are as follows: The first case: the detective is visited by a young boy, whose father has gone missing.
With the help of a local orphan, the detective investigates and finds a string of related disappearances linked to a distinguished British benefactor, a lord.
Through further inquiries, the detective discovers the lord and his aristocratic friends use paupers as hunting prey in the forest.

The father, who is a former British army marksman, uncovered this after an impoverished former squadmate of his ended up becoming quarry for the lord and his cohorts, and is now preparing to turn the tables on them during their next hunt.
The detective goes to the forest and, after avoiding the lord and his fellow hunters, he witnesses the father killing two of them and capturing the lord.

After speaking with the father, the detective can allow him to kill the lord gruesomely, kill the lord himself to give him a quick death or kill the father in order to turn the lord over to the police.
The second case: the detective competes in a lawn bowls tournament hosted by the chairman of the local archaeological society.
However, the award ceremony is called off after another member of the club, the victim, is found dead under mysterious circumstances, seemingly killed by a spear thrown by a statue of the Mayan king.

The detective investigates and finds that the victim, the chairman and the statue's maker all took part in an expedition to a tropical country 14 years prior, alongside the lost member, another club member who they claim died of illness during the expedition.

Upon investigating, the detective discovers all three survivors believed they've been cursed by the spirit of the Mayan king for having desecrated his temple and both the chairman and the statue's maker have motives to kill the victim.
The detective also uncovers that the lost member didn't die of illness as his companions claimed but rather was abandoned in the temple after accidentally triggering a trap.
Not only that, he survived, was sold into slavery and managed to return to the capital after escaping alongside another escaped slave.

The detective can either accuse the lost member; claiming he wanted revenge against his former friends for abandoning him, the chairman; claiming he wanted the victim dead so his private collection could be sold off to solvent the archeological society's near-bankrupt finances, or the statue's maker; claiming he believed killing the other survivors would rid him of the curse.
The third case: the detective is followed by the actor, an American actor set to play him in a theatrical adaptation of one of his cases.
The night after the actor's arrival, a bomb is thrown into the detective's apartment but he manages to defuse it before it goes off.

The detective looks into who may be trying to kill him and, in the process, he is recurrently forced to save the actor after he gets himself into mortal danger while trying to aid the detective's investigation.

The detective discovers the bomb was thrown by a young man, a petty crook with connections to two recently released crime bosses the detective helped arrest years prior: the first crime boss; to whom the crook frequently sells stolen goods, and the second crime boss; to whom the crook is indebted due to gambling losses.

After one final time rescuing the actor when the crook mistakes him for the detective and kidnaps him; which ultimately results in the actor killing the crook after the detective distracts him; the detective has the police bring both the first crime boss and the second crime boss into police headquarters for questioning.

After interrogating both men, the detective can accuse either one of masterminding the attempts on his life as revenge for his role in their prior arrests or he can accuse the actor, who has a strange obsession with "becoming" the detective and thus may have wanted to get rid of the real one.
The fourth case: While traveling, the detective and the doctor encounter a massive road accident that has killed and injured several people.

The detective investigates and discovers the case is more complicated than a mere accident: A gang of bankrobbers broke into a nearby bank vault via a tunnel they'd dug but, while escaping, they were electrocuted in their getaway wagon by a complex trap set up by somebody nearby, causing their wagon to stop suddenly and trigger the chain reaction that led to the massive accident.

The detective identifies three possible suspects among those in the area when the accident occurred: the activist, an anarchist activist and amateur technician; the electrician, an electrician with a sick daughter; and the construction worker, a former member of the bankrobber gang who found religion and became a construction worker.
All three suspects have varying degrees of electrical knowledge and varying degrees of proximity to the gang members.

The detective can identify any of the three suspects as the one who took part in the robbery, killed their co-conspirators and unwittingly caused the accident and either present their findings to the police or conceal them by deeming their possible motives for the crime to be justified: the activist wanted to harm an exploitative bank and dispose of the gang for preying on the poor; the electrician wanted to get the money to fund his daughter's medical treatment; and the construction worker wanted to eliminate his former gangmates because he feels guilty for having helped their past crimes.
The fifth case: the mysterious woman has kidnapped the detective's adopted daughter.
He must find her before it's too late.
The detective's reticence about the origins of his adopted daughter are revealed by the mysterious woman: the girl is the daughter of the criminal mastermind and thus the eponymous title character.
The detective pieces together that the mysterious woman is insane after finding that she keeps a spare room in a her father's crypt along with her father's mummified corpse.
The mysterious woman locks the detective in the criminal mastermind's tomb and prepares to take the girl away on a boat.
The detective escapes the tomb and finds the boat ablaze on the middle of the river.
The detective makes amends for his parental apathy and reunites with his ward.
They escape the boat as it burns and leave the mysterious woman to her death.

Taking place near the end of the 19th century and the dawn of the 20th century (known in the eastern country as the Meiji Period, in the western country as the Victorian era), the game focuses on the hero, a student at the imperial university and an ancestor of the primary protagonist of the main series.
He is described as a character with a strong sense of justice, but who easily ends up in danger.
Joining the hero is the friend, his friend from university who studies law.

The concept of defense lawyers was merely "years old" in the judicial system at the time in the eastern country, so the friend is qualified to stand in court already, and aims to transform the legal system via study in the western country.
The hero and the friend are aided by the judicial assistant, a judicial assistant.
She is described as being an "ideal Japanese woman", and is also a progressive dreamer, and a lover of foreign mystery novels.
Upon traveling to the western country to further his studies, the hero meets and befriends a world-famous British detective (given a different name in the original Japanese release).
The detective is a very eccentric and free-spirited individual.
Despite being genuinely intelligent, the rapid-fire, blasé nature of his abductive reasoning often leads the detective to incorrect conclusions.
Accompanying the detective is his assistant, the girl (given a different surname in the original Japanese release), a ten-year-old prodigy and the detective's adoptive daughter.
The girl is a genius inventor, and the author of "the stories about the detective".
In the eastern country, the hero is put on trial for the murder of a visiting university teacher, a doctor.
He is represented by his close friend, while the prosecutor is a local lawyer (the Meiji Period ancestor of a recurring character).

With help from the judicial assistant, the hero and the friend prove that the real murderer is the exchange student, an English exchange student who had been studying under the teacher at the university.
Her motive is left a mystery; she is to be sent to a neighbouring country and tried in a consular court.
Following the trial, the friend leaves the eastern country to complete his studies in the western country but hides the hero in his baggage so he can see the friend's debut in the courts.
However, while the hero is asleep, the friend is found murdered within his cabin, and the now exposed stowaway hero is once again blamed for the murder.
Working with the judicial assistant and the eccentric passenger / detective, the hero discovers that the real killer is the ballerina, a world-famous Russian ballerina who fled her homeland.

She had unintentionally killed the friend by pushing and breaking his neck on his bed's wooden knob after fearfully assuming that he was going to turn her in to the captain; in truth, he was attempting to introduce her to fellow stowaway the hero as an act of trust.
After the incident is settled, the hero persuades the judicial assistant to let him take the friend's place as a representative lawyer in the western country.
She agrees and begins to heavily tutor him on English law for the remainder of the journey.

Shortly after their arrival in the western country, the hero and the judicial assistant meet the chief justice, who assigns them the defense of the philanthropist, who has been accused of murdering the bricklayer within a moving omnibus.

They go up against the prosecutor, a legendary British prosecutor known as the "Reaper of the central court" and are introduced to the British legal system, which uses a jury of six people to decide the verdict.
During the trial, a smoke bomb is set off, forcing an evacuation of the courtroom.

After court resumes, the hero and the judicial assistant cross-examine the newly discovered witness, the young woman, and discover evidence proving that the bricklayer had been killed on the carriage roof, though the prosecutor claims that this evidence had been forged after the smoke bomb had gone off.
He is unable to prove this, and the philanthropist is subsequently acquitted, though the hero remains unsure of the philanthropist's innocence.
Shortly after the trial, the philanthropist is killed after he returns to the omnibus and it is set on fire.

The following day, the hero and the judicial assistant take on the defense of the soon to be famous Japanese novelist, who is currently in the capital studying English as a nervous exchange student, and has been charged with aggravated assault following a stabbing in the street.

During the trial, the hero proves that the stabbing was actually the result of a domestic disturbance between the landlord and his wife, who had thrown a knife at her husband, only for the knife to fall outside their window and unintentionally hit the victim.
The novelist is declared not guilty and decides that he is going to go back to the eastern country.
Meanwhile, the detective invites the hero and the judicial assistant to live with him and the girl at his lodgings and they set up their law office in their attic.
A few months later, the young woman is accused of murdering the pawnshop owner.

During the trial, where the girl aids the hero, it is revealed that the philanthropist actually was the bricklayer's murderer, and that the fire that killed the philanthropist was started by an assassin hired by the bricklayer's son, a telegraph station technician.

The technician and an unwitting bricklayer had been selling coded government secrets to the philanthropist, which eventually resulted in a fight that led to the philanthropist murdering the bricklayer; in revenge, the technician killed the philanthropist and tried to steal back the encoded secrets from the pawnshop owner's pawnshop, causing him to accidentally murder the pawnshop owner in a confrontation.

After the case is solved, the hero is suspended from practicing law due to revealing government secrets during the trial, while the judicial assistant returns to the eastern country after learning that her father is supposedly deathly ill.
Four months after the events of the first game, the young woman returns to the eastern country only to find her best friend accused of murdering the assassin, the murderer of the doctor.
Aided by her father, the young woman disguises herself as the male cousin of her friend the lawyer and proves her friend's innocence by outing the real murderer, a journalist.

After the trial, she finds out that her father did not have a deathly illness and that her return home was due to a case she and the lawyer handled in the western country six months ago: while proving the client innocent of the poisoning of a failed actor, the pair discovered a jewelled dog collar in the client's apartment, stained in dried blood, but were forced by the detective to hand it over to the police, advising them and his assistant the girl to not disclose any details of their discovery.

The young woman returns to the western country, where an explosion at the demonstration of an experimental teleportation device results in its inventor being held responsible for the death of a known crime lord who had financed the machine.
The lawyer, seeking to defend him, receives permission from the chief justice to return to court after a six month absence from the courtroom.

Facing off against the infamous prosecutor — who holds a reputation as the "Reaper" for the defendants he prosecutes dying even if found innocent — he discovers the case is linked to a spate of serial killings ten years prior conducted with a dog handled by an individual called the "Professor", whose final victim was the prosecutor's brother.

The lawyer proves the victim was murdered by the police's chief coroner, who was being blackmailed over fabricating evidence concerning the Professor's alleged execution. The prosecutor reveals to the lawyer and the young woman that the Professor was a Japanese man, while the prosecutor's masked protégé reveals himself as an amnesiac friend, the lawyer's best friend who was presumed dead months ago.
The protégé recovers his memories upon seeing a waxwork of the Professor, who he recognizes as his father.
Days later, the police inspector is murdered while investigating an outfit called the league.
Despite their rivalry, the lawyer comes to the prosecutor's defense when he is arrested as the prime suspect.
However, he finds himself surprised to be facing off against the protégé, who has accepted the case as its prosecutor.
Due to the nature of the case, an order is given for the trial to be closed to the public, resulting in no jury being present.

As the trial commences, the lawyer discovers that the protégé came to the western country to investigate the prosecutor, whom he blames for the protégé's father being accused of the Professor killings and executed.
When a witness collapses after it transpires that they aided the protégé's father's jailbreak, the trial is suspended to allow for further investigation into the matter.

As the trial resumes, with the chief justice presiding over it as judge, the detective's investigation into the case, aided by the young woman's father — revealed to be his partner and not the doctor, as the girl had assumed — leads the lawyer to discover that the Japanese Minister of Foreign Affairs murdered the police inspector on the chief justice's orders, and that the chief justice was the mastermind behind both the Professor and Reaper killings.

Admitting to the truth, the chief justice claims he was trying to create a crime-free western country, using the prosecutor's brother as the Professor, initially to kill corrupt members of society, before conscripting the assassin to kill the prosecutor's defendants.

When the protégé's father discovered the truth and killed the prosecutor's brother in a duel, he threatened to use a confession written by the prosecutor's brother to expose the chief justice, but was later murdered by the minister on the chief justice's orders when his fake execution was accidentally uncovered by mistake.

Unable to find the confession amongst the protégé's father's possessions, the chief justice framed the protégé's father for the Professor killings, and ten years later had both the doctor and the police inspector, who forged the Professor's autopsy, murdered to avoid the truth coming out.

Despite the lawyer and the protégé finding the confession on a missing page of the prosecutor's brother's will hidden in the protégé's father's katana, the chief justice declares he is untouchable, but the detective arrives with news that the Queen has learned of the chief justice's crimes and ordered his arrest.

With the trial resolved, the young woman's father reveals to the lawyer that the girl is actually the prosecutor's brother's daughter, not the doctor's, and that he and the detective hid this knowledge from her for her protection.
After making peace with both the prosecutor and the protégé, who decides to remain a prosecutor, the lawyer returns to the eastern country with the young woman.
In October 1889, the detective's brother the government official is injured in an explosion when his club, the gentlemen's club, is blown up.
The player, first as the doctor and then as the detective, investigates the explosion and discovers that it was not a gas leak but a bomb which was the cause.
In an encrypted note, the government official writes to the detective that a chemical formula for an extremely powerful explosive had recently been stolen from the defence ministry.
Though the defence ministry, at the government official's instigation, opens an investigation regarding the theft, it's quickly and suspiciously closed by its committee members.

The detective and the doctor trail various suspects provided by the government official, ranging from an impoverished aristocrat and an ambitious defence ministry clerk to an eccentric magnate and a politically active charlady.

The gruesome murder of what turns out to be a member of an exclusive university student society links the case to the machinations of a Prussian military officer who covertly tries to advance the cause of the chancellor at the expense of the emperor in a conspiracy that involved the theft of the formula, as well as the kidnapping and blackmail of investigation committee to hush up the aftermath.
The detective ultimately neutralises the conspiracy, tracks down the culprits and recovers the lost documents.
In the epilogue, the detective receives a knighthood from the queen, who asks him to keep the accolade a secret.

The plot is separate from the previous game, the earlier instalment, though multiple characters return from that game, such as characters from the author's detective stories like the inspector of the police headquarters, as well as some minor characters original to the games like the police sergeant, the desk sergeant at the police headquarters.
The year is 1887, and all of the country is gearing up for the celebration of the queen's golden jubilee, marking her 50th year as monarch.
The city, naturally, is especially frenzied.
Reading the paper one morning, the detective seizes upon one seemingly unimportant notice: The fortress has been closed for "reasons of security".
The great detective is unsurprised when, moments later, he is asked to investigate the theft of the royal jewels.
The clues left behind, however, positively reek of a carefully laid trap; the detective decides that he must step aside and allow the doctor to pursue the thief instead.
If the jewels are not replaced within 48 hours, the British government will be forced to admit that their most prized possessions were stolen and suffer worldwide humiliation.

The player fills the role of the doctor, travelling around the city in horse-drawn cabs while attempting to recover the royal jewels while encountering many characters from the author's stories such as the landlady, the detective's brother, and the street urchin of the gang of street boys.
A series of riddles and clues lead the doctor on a hunt for inscribed jewels hidden at several famous sites across the city, including the abbey, the wax museum, the bridge, and the clock tower.
Eventually, the villain is revealed as the criminal mastermind, who captures both the doctor and the detective.
With quick thinking and the help of some humble medical supplies, however, the doctor manages to subdue the criminal mastermind and return the royal jewels to the fortress in time.
In the city, 1898, a newspaper article accuses the detective of the theft of a priceless set of jewels.
With no solid evidence, the inspector says he will investigate further.
The detective tells the doctor he has an immediate appointment with the bishop.
Upon arriving, he discovers that the bishop has been tied up, burnt and mutilated.
The detective deduces that the culprits had been low class workers, who had been hired and given a special poison that caused a form of psychotic madness.
The detective goes to the prison in order to interview the convict, a convicted poisoner.
A fire begins in the cellblocks, during which the convict escapes.
It is implied that the detective helped him escape in return for information about the poisoning case.
The detective and the doctor discover the poison was administered through tainted opium from an opium den in the poor district.
The detective wants to question the Bishop's nephew, the young man.
With the help of tracking dog the hound, they track the young man to his hideout at the wharf and find him within a smelting plant.
The young man holds the detective at gunpoint, but the hound accidentally knocks him into a vat of molten metal, killing him.
With the trail dead, the detective returns to the theft of the necklace.
The detective breaks into the office of the newspaperman, a journalist who seems intent on proving the detective is a fraud.
Using his deductive powers, the detective discovers that the newspaperman has recently been visited by local judge the magistrate.
The detective and the doctor break into the magistrate's house.
The detective leaves a mysterious package on the magistrate's desk.
They discover that the magistrate has a collection of evidence against the detective, making the doctor suspicious.
The doctor spots the magistrate and insists on talking to him.
The detective says that he is leaving, but the doctor stays, and approaches the house, which suddenly explodes, causing the doctor to be knocked out cold.
The detective disappears, and is now wanted for questioning about the explosion.
The doctor finds the detective hiding at a rented room in the poor district.
The detective tells the doctor he is heading out of the city to continue the investigation.
They arrive at a sawmill inhabited by three Russian anarchists.
One of them warns that the detective is dangerous and shouldn't be trusted.
The inspector and the police arrive to look for the detective.
The doctor informs them the detective is upstairs.
The inspector goes after him alone and is soon thrown from the window.
Now branded a murderer, the detective stages his own death and goes back into hiding.
The doctor tracks him down, where the detective reveals everything he knows.

The criminal mastermind has been plotting to cause panic by poisoning the poor of the city, thus destabilising the government and creating a massive power vacuum, which the criminal mastermind would fill with a puppet ruler loyal only to him.
Knowing the detective was the only one that could stop his plan, the criminal mastermind recruited the inspector to help discredit him.
As the magistrate had started growing suspicious of the inspector's evidence against the detective, the criminal mastermind ordered his home bombed to further frame the detective.

The detective and the doctor go to the criminal mastermind's hideout, where they discover the three Russian anarchists have made bombs that will go off via radio transmitter at key locations including the police headquarters.
The detective learns that the criminal mastermind is not in control of the scheme.
After disconnecting the bombs from the radio transmitter, the detective and the doctor use another bomb to destroy the factory.
It is revealed that the convict was the power behind the criminal mastermind.
Under the influence of his own poison, the convict attacks the criminal mastermind and savagely bites at his throat.
The criminal mastermind shoots him, but is too late to save himself.
With his dying breath, the criminal mastermind asks the detective to take care of his daughter, as he is the only one worthy to teach her.
In July 1895, the detective and the doctor receive a letter from the legendary French gentleman thief the burglar.
The burglar threatens to steal five of the country's most prized treasures in hopes to humble the "vanity" of the English, and leaves a riddle containing information on what his first crime will be.

The detective and the doctor determine that the theft will take place at the art gallery, and upon arriving there deduce that the object will be the famous painting, which is symbolic of the country's victory over the burglar's homeland and its ally in the famous naval battle.
They alert the Museum Director and the inspector who has the art gallery guarded at every entrance.
However, the next morning, they find the guards knocked out and the painting stolen.
The detective learns that the burglar disguised himself as a visiting French painter, and hid before the inspector arrived.
The burglar leaves behind a letter with a clue as to where he will strike next.
The detective and the doctor head to the fortress, where they believe the burglar will steal the ravens.
They arrived too late, as the ravens are reported missing and replaced with other individual birds and a bat which have been let loose.
They capture the animals and find pieces of paper attached to them.
From the messages in the papers, the detective deduces what the burglar will do next.

The detective and the doctor meet with the inspector and the Prime Minister at the national museum where the detective informs them that the burglar intends to steal the ancient inscribed stone, which was taken by the country from the French.
The inspector once again has the national museum guarded at every entrance but the burglar still manages to steal the stone right in front of them using ropes.
He leaves behind yet another letter.
The detective determines that someone had unwittingly helped the burglar pass the security system.
Unknown to him, the doctor had befriended a man claiming to be a journalist, whom he helped into the museum to pay him back for some favours.
The doctor soon confesses and the detective deduces, to his horror, that the burglar's next target will be the queen herself.
At the royal palace, the detective and the doctor find that the Prime Minister has had the place guarded heavily.
The detective learns that a French grandfather clock (which has a cupboard) was delivered to the queen's chamber and correctly deduces that the burglar made it to the queen.
The burglar, however, does not hurt her but asks for a kiss which she obliges.
She then allows him to use her secret corridor to escape.
The detective pursues the burglar but only manages to find another letter which clues to his next and final crime.
The Prime Minister congratulates the detective and the doctor for their role in protecting the Queen and asks the doctor to decipher the burglar's message.
The doctor initially deduces that the next crime will be at the fortress but the Prime Minister reminds him that the burglar already struck there.
The doctor then determines that the final target will be the clock tower.
The doctor joins the Prime Minister, the inspector and much of the police force to wait for the burglar there but the detective goes to the fortress.
He learns that the burglar's past four crimes were distractions from his real target, the royal jewels.
The detective sabotages the burglar's plan and confronts him.
The two express their mutual admiration.
The burglar agrees to return the stolen items and the detective lets him go, knowing they will not see each other again.
The detective later tells the doctor not to write about this endeavor.
